---
package: "openpipeline_composed"
version: "v0.3.0"
title: "parallel_integration"
subtitle: "openpipeline_composed v0.3.0"
toc: true
namespace: "Single cell"
description: "Run multiple integration methods from OpenPipeline in parallel on the same preprocessed h5mu input, then merge each method's annotations (leiden cluster labels in .obs, integrated embeddings and UMAPs in .obsm, neighbor graphs in .obsp and .uns) back into a single output h5mu."
type: "workflow"
latest: "true"
---

::: {.column-margin}

Which modality to process.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"rna"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--layer_log_normalized_counts`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Layer with the log-normalized counts. Read by the methods that operate
on normalized expression: harmony, scanorama and bbknn.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"log_normalized"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--layer_raw_counts`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Layer with the raw (integer) counts. Read by scVI, which requires raw
counts rather than log-normalized data. If left unset, scVI reads the
counts from the modality's .X.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obsm_embedding`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.obsm slot containing the embedding to use as input for methods that
require a pre-computed dimensionality reduction (harmony, scanorama, bbknn).
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"X_pca"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_batch`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.obs column discriminating between batches. Read by scVI, scanorama and bbknn.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"sample_id"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_covariates`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.obs column(s) defining the covariates to regress out. Read by harmony.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"sample_id"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_categorical_covariates`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.obs column(s) with categorical covariates for scVI to correct for in
addition to --obs_batch. Treated as nuisance factors, so do not use them
for biological signal you want to keep. None by default.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_numerical_covariates`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.obs column(s) with continuous (numerical) covariates for scVI to correct
for in addition to --obs_batch. Treated as nuisance factors, so do not use
them for biological signal you want to keep. None by default.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--var_input`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.var column containing highly variable genes to subset to. Read by scVI.
By default, scVI uses all genes.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::

### Output slot naming

Names of the slots each method writes into its intermediate h5mu and
that are subsequently moved into the merged output. The per-resolution
leiden columns are named "{obs_cluster}_{resolution}" (e.g.
"harmony_integration_leiden_1.0").

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline_composed \
  -r v0.3.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/single_cell/parallel_integration/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline_composed/v0.3.0/components/single_cell/parallel_integration);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline_composed \
  -r v0.3.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/single_cell/parallel_integration/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
